insights.title: Soaring Petrol Prices Driving Inflation Surge
insights.description: Petrol prices increased 143.9% over one year (from 8.2 to 20), while inflation rose from 42000 to 55000 (30.95% increase). The root cause is likely supply-side shocks or currency devaluation, as petrol price hikes directly feed into inflation. If unchecked, this could lead to stagflation, reduced consumer spending, and economic contraction.
insights.root_cause: Supply-side constraints or currency devaluation causing rapid petrol price increases, which propagate through the economy as higher inflation.
insights.forward_implication: Without intervention, inflation will continue to rise, eroding purchasing power and potentially triggering a recession.

temporal_signals.change_description: Increased 143.9% from 8.2 to 20 over one year (2025-10-2 to 2026-10-2).
